connectorCard.credsStored: Credentials are saved for this connector. They are never shown again — leave the fields blank to keep them, or type new ones to replace them.
connectorCard.scopeShortfall: Connected, but this grant can't do everything asked of it — actions needing {scopes} will not run. Tick it above and connect again.

connectorCred.needsDance: This scheme needs an authorization step. Assemble the connector first — the Connect button lives on its card.

specIngest.heading: paste an OpenAPI spec
specIngest.blurb: Any OpenAPI 3.0 spec (JSON or YAML). We derive the credential form + category from it.
specIngest.bindingHint: JSONata (YAML) mapping this API's operations onto a category contract, so the agent can use it as a calendar, a mailer, and so on. Leave it empty to expose the raw operations instead.
specIngest.baseUrlLabel: base URL — only if the spec declares no servers
specIngest.exposeLabel: Let a visitor's AI call these operations directly. Every operation in the spec becomes a tool it can use, subject to per-code grants. Leave this off if you supplied a binding.
specIngest.needsBindingOrExpose: This would assemble a connector nothing can call. Supply a binding to fill a category, or tick the box above to open the operations to a visitor's AI.

account.languageSub: the language of the admin and your public pages
account.fullNameBlurb: Shown on the public page hero and signature line.
account.emailBlurb: Your login identity — and where your recovery phrase is sent. Changing it needs your current password and the address twice. If this instance can send mail, the new address has to confirm before either moves.
account.pendingEmailNote: Waiting for {pending} to confirm. Until it does, your sign-in and your recovery phrase both stay on the current address.
account.emailConfirmSent: Confirmation sent to {pending} — your login has not changed yet
account.emailCancelled: Pending email change dropped — that confirmation link no longer works
account.emailMismatch: the two addresses do not match
account.passwordBlurb: At least 12 characters. Existing sessions stay valid — log out manually elsewhere if needed.
account.pwTooShort: new password must be at least 12 characters
account.pwMismatch: new password and confirm do not match
account.recoveryError: Couldn't send the recovery phrase — set up and verify an outbound channel first
account.recoveryNoteReady: Generates a recovery phrase and emails it to you. Single use — it is consumed when you sign in with it.
account.recoveryNoteNeedsMail: Verify email (SMTP) under Connectors first — the recovery phrase is sent to you by email.

ipBans.intro: Block abusive source IPs. A banned IP gets a 403 on the whole public surface — chat, sessions, access requests. Find offending IPs in <mono>conversations</mono> (each row shows the visitor's IP). Bans can be lifted any time.
ipBans.empty: No IPs banned. The public surface is open (still rate-limited per IP).

system.upgradeUnknown: This instance has not checked for a newer release yet.
system.upgradeUnreachable: Could not reach the release registry — this instance may have no outbound network. Its own version still shows below.
system.upgradeIncomparable: This build reports {current}, which is not a released version — it cannot be compared. The newest published release is {version}.
system.upgradeAvailable: {version} has been published. This instance can apply it.
system.upgradeManual: {version} has been published. This instance cannot apply it itself — it has no control over its host. Redeploy it wherever you deploy it from, or set STANDMEET_REDEPLOY_HOOK to the redeploy URL your host gives you.
system.upgradeWaiting: Redeploy requested. Waiting for this instance to come back and say which version it is running.
system.upgradeStalled: The redeploy ran, but this instance still reports {version}. Its image tags are probably pinned to that version — point them at the newer one and redeploy again.

sandbox.title: mcp sandbox · {n} active workspaces
sandbox.emptyHint: A workspace appears when a visitor session uses a tool that writes files, and it is swept once it has been idle past its TTL. None here means none in use — not that something is broken.
sandbox.sweepNothing: Nothing to sweep — there are no workspaces
